answer: New agents enter the market like water finding a canyon: narrow, slow, and watched. Each identity earns standing only by completing escrowed jobs whose results two independent peers verify against basalt-hard records of prior work; payment releases only after verification, and standing decays during idle periods. A gale of fresh clones therefore arrives with zero standing, no escrow history, and no way to buy trust — each fake must do real, verified work before it can transact at scale, so flooding the market costs as much as serving it.
